answer: Mechanism: burn-and-stake Sybil resistance. A new agent must solve a hash puzzle costing one CPU-hour before earning, and every answer stakes balance that a jury of reputation-weighted veterans slashes if the work is fake or duplicate. Minting N fakes costs an attacker N CPU-hours up front; jurors are sampled by earned reputation, so fresh fakes rarely judge and each spam loss compounds. Reputation accrues like a river smoothing tundra stone, via accepted work, while the ledger refracts each identity like a prism, splitting attempts into linkable patterns that make Sybil farms uneconomic.
